text:
mike: Heads up — after rolling kernel 6.x to a subset of p4 hosts in us-west2 we started seeing repeated nvidia module reloads and OOMs. Hosts are dropping into degraded and GPUs show as offline.

sara: Ugh. Which kbranch and drivers? any error snippets? :eyes:

mike: Kernel 6.4.2 -> 6.4.9 delta. Driver 525.116.04 (dkms). dmesg sample pasted below.

mike: ```
[ 1123.456789] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: IOMMU mapping fault on read access, addr:0x7f4a3c000 len:4
[ 1123.457012] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: MMU fault: reason 'access violation'
[ 1123.457333] nvidia: probe of 0000:3b:00.0 failed with error -12
[ 1123.457899] Out of memory: Kill process 21456 (nvidia-modul) score 987 or sacrifice child
```

leo: The -12 probe fail plus OOM smells like DKMS modules built against 6.4 headers are stomping on a kernel allocator path. We saw similar on a canary last week but didn’t catch the pattern.

ashley: Also seeing NCCL issues — jobs report handshake timeouts and long allreduce stalls when this starts. Could be nvlink + driver state flapping -> NCCL retries -> memory growth.

oncall-bot: alert: 8 hosts in us-west2-p4 pool marked degraded in the last 10m (auto-evacuate triggered). Incident ticket created: INF-4521.

mike: Confirmed: 8 hosts, 24 GPUs affected. Evacuation is working but capacity is strained, queue backlog rising ~30% and some CI jobs stuck.

sara: Can we get the kernel boot param / module list from one affected host? Also paste lsmod | grep nvidia output.

mike: ```
# uname -r
6.4.9-rt1
# lsmod | grep nvidia
nvidia_drm 49152 3
nvidia_modeset 286720 4
nvidia 1826048 250
```

mike: But dmesg also shows `nvidia_uvm` leaking contexts and not unloading even after processes exit.

leo: Two possible mitigation paths: (A) rollback kernel to 6.4.2 on the affected pool (fast but needs coord with kprov), (B) force-rebuild dkms drivers against the new headers with extra CONFIG flags and reboot (longer). Which do we prefer?

ashley: Rollback seems fastest for immediate stability. We should pin nodes in warm pool and progressively roll. Need oncall to approve a rollback-window.

infra-sre: We prefer a staged rollback: 4 hosts first, monitor 30m, then remainder. Can we hotfix a kernel module blacklist or `modprobe --remove-dependencies` scripted fallback? Not safe unless we confirm no user workloads.

mike: I'll prepare a drain+rollback playbook. Quick note: temp workaround found in upstream mailing list — add `nvidia.NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers=1` to module parameters reduces UVM allocation churn in some 6.x combos. Worth testing on one host.

sara: Good call. Test that on a single host with repro job. If it stabilizes, we can push as a config patch while rolling back kernel.

oncall-bot: reminder: runbook step 3 -> set `fleetctl drain --reason "kernel-6x-nv-reload"` then `imagectl rollback-kernel --target 6.4.2` (requires 2 approvals).

leo: Who has approval? ops lead + infra lead. @sara and @ashley can you sign off?

ashley: I approve emergency rollback for that pool.

sara: I approve. Go ahead, mike, execute the staged rollback and report status in this thread. :white_check_mark:

mike: Starting staged rollback on 4 hosts now. Will paste progress and watch NCCL latencies.

mike: Host g-ww-034: drained -> rollback started -> restart -> back online. GPUs green.

mike: Host g-ww-035: rollback failed on one host, dkms recompile error during boot, collecting logs.

mike: ```
[FAILED] dkms build for nvidia-525: kernel 6.4.2 header mismatch: cannot find /usr/src/linux-headers-6.4.2
```

leo: If headers mismatch we need to ensure package sync — provisioning may have mixed kernel/header versions. Add step to verify `apt-get install linux-headers-$(uname -r)` before reboot.

mike: Will patch the playbook. For now we have 3/4 rolled back and cluster load is easing. Queue backlog down 18%.

ashley: Open items: (1) fleetwide audit for kernel/header/drivers parity, (2) postmortem INF-4521 with root cause triage, (3) validate upstream driver 525 + 6.4.x compatibility matrix before future rollouts.

infra-sre: Also need to flag region tgts — us-west2 had narrower spare capacity which amplified impact. Recommend temporary capacity increases during kernel window.

sara: I'll start the postmortem doc and collect logs (dmesg, /var/log/kern.log, nvidia-smi topo, dkms status). Add repro test to release gate: run kube-e2e NCCL stress job against canary pool pre-rollout.

mike: Thanks. Will keep monitoring and post final status once full pool restored or rollback completes.

oncall-bot: incident INF-4521 status: in_progress -> assigned to mike.

mike: Final note for runbook: add `preflight: verify linux-headers, dkms status, nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,serial --format=csv` as gating checks.

ashley: Great. If anything flares up ping infra pager. Closing for now but keep thread open for updates. :lock:
